To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we experimentally demonstrate a quantum-controlled-phase gate for continuous-variables using a cluster state of four optical modes and that we verify that it works by showing the presence of genuine entanglement at its output for a product coherent input state.
we have demonstrated a controlled-phase gate that is entangling and that it is compatible with the one-way quantum computation scheme.

we experimentally demonstrate a teleportation-based implementation of a controlled-phase two-mode gate for continuous variables, and that this gate, together with a module for single-mode operations, can be used as a universal resource for measurement-based continuous-variable quantum computation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the experimental demonstration of a continuous-variable controlled-phase gate.
the development of a new quantum computing model that uses continuous-variable cluster states as a resource and measurements as a universal set of operations.
the development of new methods for the manipulation of quantum information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work represents the first step toward a fully measurement-based continuous-variable quantum computation.
the experiment is a proof-of-principle for the feasibility of continuous-variable one-way computation.
our work demonstrates the first experimental implementation of a controlled-phase entangling gate for continuous variables.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the present experiment represents a step forward in demonstrating a universal quantum computation scheme based on continuous variables, which is a promising alternative to discrete-variable approaches.
we demonstrate a quantum gate for continuous variables that can be used to implement any multimodal Gaussian unitary operation as a one-way quantum computation.

, in addition to the already demonstrated single-mode Gaussian gates, we now have a controlled-phase gate, and therefore, we can implement any multimode operation in the Gaussian domain as a fully measurement based quantum computation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cluster-state approach is applicable to continuous variables and that the resulting measurement-based scheme can be used to perform universal continuous-variable quantum computation.
the quantum information processing capabilities of Gaussian states and Gaussian operations can now be exploited in a measurement-based fashion.
a single cluster state is enough to implement any multimodes Gaussian operation.
